checks.name: Eval rows that also appear in training data (needs row hashes)
checks.message: 12 of 9768 evaluation rows (0.12%) also appear in the training row hashes. Datasets can contain genuine duplicate records (0.03% of evaluation rows duplicate another evaluation row), so a small overlap is not by itself leakage. The hashes are producer-supplied.

checks.name: Highest ROC AUC reached by any single feature on eval data
checks.message: The strongest single feature, 'relationship', reaches a cross-validated ROC AUC of 0.772 on its own (12 features, 9768 rows). Values near 1.0 suggest the feature leaks the label.

details.caveat: A legitimately strong feature also scores high; leakage spread over several features is not detected.

checks.name: Evaluation rows whose features are identical to another row's but whose label differs
checks.message: 0 of 9768 evaluation rows (0.00%) share their feature values with a row that has a different label (0 conflicting groups among 3 groups of repeated feature values). Conflicting labels put a ceiling on the accuracy any model can reach and make the measured metrics unreliable.

details.caveat: Only exact repeats of the feature values are found, so data with continuous features has little power; the gate cannot check the training labels, which it does not receive.

checks.name: Training rows that duplicate another training row (from the supplied row hashes)
checks.message: 17 of 29305 training rows (0.06%) duplicate another training row. Duplicates can make a model look better on rows it has memorised and are often a data-quality problem upstream. The hashes are producer-supplied and cover the feature columns only, so rows with the same features and different labels also count as duplicates.

details.caveat: The gate does not see the training data, only its row hashes.
